title: Adaptive hotspot tiering and probabilistic shard reclamation for paged-attention KV
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: In high-concurrency hosted workloads we observe short-lived token hot-spots that cause repeated KV page churn, decode stalls, and tail-latency spikes. Current LRU-style reclaim and static shard sizing lead to fragmentation and expensive rehydrates. Goal: design and ship an adaptive two-tier residency + probabilistic shard reclamation protocol that reduces tail latency and rehydration work for paged-attention KV without increasing median cost. The design combines: 1) lightweight hot-spot detection (per-shard bloom + short decay counters), 2) a fast local-tier (small resident microcache) for ephemeral hot spans, 3) a background probabilistic reclaim for cold shards that avoids full-page compaction in the fast path, and 4) prefill-aware admission that biases kernel placement (e.g., prefetched pages pinned to decode-optimized kernels). Success metrics: 30% reduction in 99th token latency on representative chat workloads, 20% fewer full-page rehydrates, and <=3% median cost uplift. Scope: runtime allocator, shard metadata, prefill admission hook, kernel hint propagation, and observability (per-tenant hotness gauges and reclaim counters).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes per-shard hotness metric and tiered residency counts
Background probabilistic reclaim runs with configurable aggressiveness and avoids decode-path stalls
Prefill admission pins prefetched spans to resident microcache for the next N requests
End-to-end benchmark: <=30% reduction in 99th token latency on internal chat workload compared to baseline
No regression on median cost and throughput in the dedicated tier tests
implementation_notes: Key pieces: 1) Hotness sampling — small bloom per shard updated in prefill and decode; decay ticks implemented in scheduler; 2) Microcache — fixed-size per-GPU slab of recently touched micro-spans with tag-based lookup to avoid hash-table cost; 3) Reclaim — probabilistic per-shard sampling that evicts candidate micro-spans and only triggers heavy compaction if sampled cold repeatedly; 4) Kernel hints — prefill admission emits a kernel preference tag attached to spans so kernel-selector can prefer low-latency prefetch-optimized kernels; 5) Metrics — hotness, microcache hit rate, reclaim samples, rehydrate events; all available in Console and per-route dashboards.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed — measured hot-spot dwell time distribution across 10 live tenant traces (median dwell 4 requests, 95th 18 requests).
2025-02-18: Prototype microcache implemented in experiment branch (ENG-384217-microcache-spike). Synthetic microbench shows 12% 99p token latency reduction for single-tenant bursty traffic.
2025-02-22: Design review with runtime and kernel teams. Action: add kernel hinting path and ensure prefill admission is non-blocking. Miguel to prototype kernel-tag propagation by 2025-02-28.

2025-02-28: Integration test harness updated to simulate cross-tenant eviction pressure. Observed increased fragmentation on older slabs — added conservative decay and a soft reserve quota per-tenant to avoid noisy eviction.

2025-03-01: Security review requested (KMS not involved). Edge-case noted: tenant-weighted microcache starvation when tenant weights change rapidly — created follow-up ENG-384998 to address fair share admission.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Probabilistic reclaim may under-evict during long sustained bursts, increasing memory pressure. Mitigation: add a reactive fallback that escalates to deterministic reclamation when overall residency exceeds threshold.
Risk: Kernel hinting could create kernel hot-path imbalance. Mitigation: kernel-selector includes capacity-aware scoring and will ignore hints if target kernel is saturated.
Risk: Increased control-plane telemetry cost. Mitigation: sample metrics for high-cardinality tenants and provide an opt-in high-resolution mode for debug runs.
review_feedback: PM (Lena Hoffman): Ensure the SLO guardrails are explicit — define the cost safety budget and rollback triggers.
Kernel lead (Jing Wu): Prefer a kernel-hint fingerprint over full span tags to keep scheduling inexpensive.
Security (Marco Silva): No secrets handled but request that audit logs capture aggressive reclaim escalations.
next_steps: Finish kernel-hint prototype and add unit tests (target: 2025-03-07)
Merge microcache fast-path behind runtime feature flag and run perf gate in stage (target: 2025-03-10)
Evaluate results on 10% of traffic via canary with automatic rollback if 99p latency regresses beyond threshold
